claims.text: The starting material is an as-deposited sputtered, non-equiatomic FeMnNiGeSi-type high-entropy-alloy thin film.
The as-deposited film has an ordered, single-phase hexagonal structure.
The as-deposited film exhibits a sharp, hysteretic, first-order magnetostructural transition.
The intervention is vacuum annealing at 850 K for 30 minutes followed by rapid quenching in an inert-gas atmosphere.
Annealing and quenching will refine the film microstructure and increase its grain-boundary density.
The treatment will modify the distribution of defects.
The treated film will retain the single-phase hexagonal structure.
Grain boundaries act as spatially distributed nucleation sites for the magnetostructural transition.
Increasing the density of grain-boundary nucleation sites spreads the transformation over a broader temperature range.
A spatially distributed transformation reduces abrupt energy-barrier crossing associated with hysteresis.
The treated films will exhibit a broader magnetocaloric transition than the as-deposited controls.
The treated films will exhibit less hysteresis than the as-deposited controls.
The treated films will have a slightly lower peak entropy change than the as-deposited controls.
The reduced peak entropy change will remain acceptable for magnetic cooling.
The comparison will be performed under applied fields no greater than 0.2 T.
The predicted effect depends on optimizing annealing temperature, duration, and quenching rate so that grain-boundary density is enhanced without secondary-phase formation.
Excessive processing can compromise magnetocaloric capacity.
